## Summary by CodeRabbit

## Walkthrough

This PR updates bin/convert/types.ts: adds an import for tryAsTimeSlot, expands the "stf-vector" SUPPORTED_TYPES options to include "as-block-fuzz-message" and "as-state-fuzz-message", emits a deprecation warning for the old "as-fuzz-message" option, and implements new branches. "as-state-fuzz-message" builds a v1.Initialize using test.pre_state.keyvals and an ancestry entry derived from test.block.header with a time-slot via tryAsTimeSlot. "as-block-fuzz-message" encodes and wraps a fuzz Block message. A small .coderabbit.yaml rule was also added.

The removal of `as-fuzz-message` from the `stf-vector` command and replacement with `as-block-fuzz-message` and `as-state-fuzz-message` is a breaking change. Any code or scripts using `stf-vector as-fuzz-message` will fail.

**Potential underflow: handle timeSlotIndex = 0 case.**

Line 224 computes `test.block.header.timeSlotIndex - 1` without checking if `timeSlotIndex` is 0. Since `timeSlotIndex` is a `TimeSlot` (opaque U32), subtracting 1 when the value is 0 produces -1, which will cause `tryAsTimeSlot(tryAsU32(-1))` to throw a runtime error.

This issue would occur when processing genesis blocks or blocks at slot 0.



<details>
<summary>🛡️ Proposed fix to handle the edge case</summary>

Consider adding a boundary check:

```diff
         if (option === "as-state-fuzz-message") {
+          const ancestry = test.block.header.timeSlotIndex > 0
+            ? [
+                v1.AncestryItem.create({
+                  headerHash: test.block.header.parentHeaderHash,
+                  slot: tryAsTimeSlot(test.block.header.timeSlotIndex - 1),
+                }),
+              ]
+            : [];
           const init = v1.Initialize.create({
             header: Header.empty(),
             keyvals: test.pre_state.keyvals,
-            ancestry: [
-              v1.AncestryItem.create({
-                headerHash: test.block.header.parentHeaderHash,
-                slot: tryAsTimeSlot(test.block.header.timeSlotIndex - 1),

+            ancestry,
           });

             type: v1.MessageType.Initialize,
             value: init,
           };
           return looseType({
             value: msg,
             encode: v1.messageCodec,
           });
         }
```

This ensures that blocks at slot 0 produce an empty ancestry array (similar to the stf-genesis handler at line 160), while later blocks correctly reference their parent.
</details>

      /**
       * Create a new [`Decoder`] instance from given bytes blob and starting offset.
       */
      static fromBytesBlob(source: BytesBlob, offset?: number) {

      }

      /**
       * Create a new [`Decoder`] instance given a raw array of bytes as a source.
       */
      static fromBlob(source: Uint8Array, context?: unknown) {
        return new Decoder(source, undefined, context);
      }

      /**
       * Decode a single object from all of the source bytes.
       *
       * NOTE that if you need to decode multiple objects, it might be better
       * to create a [`Decoder`] instance intstead of slicing the data.
       */
      static decodeObject<T>(decode: Decode<T>, source: BytesBlob | Uint8Array, context?: unknown): T {
        const decoder = source instanceof BytesBlob ? Decoder.fromBytesBlob(source) : Decoder.fromBlob(source);
        decoder.attachContext(context);
        const obj = decoder.object(decode);
        decoder.finish();
        return obj;

          } else {
            assertNever(action);

      getRootHash(blake2b: Blake2b): StateRootHash {
        const blake2bTrieHasher = getBlake2bTrieHasher(blake2b);
        const leaves: SortedSet<LeafNode> = SortedSet.fromArray(leafComparator);
        for (const [key, value] of this) {
          leaves.insert(InMemoryTrie.constructLeaf(blake2bTrieHasher, key.asOpaque(), value));
        }
    
        return InMemoryTrie.computeStateRoot(blake2bTrieHasher, leaves).asOpaque();
